doc: Cells confirmed, via live verification, to have NO real path forward -- the gap tool's own heuristics would otherwise keep re-flagging these as 'sourced-not-built'/'walled'/'no source known' on every regeneration, costing real investigation time to re-derive the same answer. Each entry needs: state, county (or null for every county in that state), column, reason (specific, falsifiable), confirmed_date, confidence ('high' = directly verified for this exact cell; 'medium' = inferred from a verified sibling/structural rule, not independently re-checked for every county it covers). gap_matrix.py's roll_up() checks this registry before finalizing each cell's gap_class and overrides to 'declined (<reason>)' when found -- never silently; the override is itself visible in the gap list so a human can challenge it. A declined entry is a claim, not a law: if new evidence contradicts one (the underlying platform adds a field, a law changes, a county switches vendors), remove or correct the entry and re-verify live before trusting the correction.

Its only bulk GIS layer (Pickens_Open_data FeatureServer/6) has no value field of any kind; its alternate platform (Catalis/Sturgis) only extracts Appraised/Assessed and its CDN API returns a live HTTP 403 (confirmed CatalisBlocked wall).

Its tax card's 'Land Market Value' vs 'Land Use Value' split looks like an ag-deferral field but live-checking 5 real parcel cards showed the split appears on ordinary RESIDENTIAL IMPROVED parcels too (not just FARM VACANT) -- it's a structural artifact of the acreage-valuation schedule (any parcel with a Gross Acres land record gets both numbers), not an ag-rollback flag. No 'Deferred'/'Rollback' label exists on the card. Would need an ACTUAL deferred/rollback label to change this, not a re-derivation from the Market/Use split.

Both GIS hosts (gis2.orangeburgcounty.org, arcserver2.orangeburgcounty.org) have been down/connection-refused for 13+ days (re-confirmed 2026-10-21, not a blip); qPublic is CAPTCHA-walled; the only live AGOL replica has owner/mailing/acreage only, no value or land-use field.

Its cached TOTBDGVAL (building-value-only) field looked like a clean $0=vacant signal (35% of parcels), but a live satellite spot-check against real addresses found actual rooftops on 2 of 7 checked $0 parcels -- almost certainly manufactured/mobile homes taxed as separate personal property, excluded from the real-property improvement-value card. Wiring TOTBDGVAL as vacant_lot here would mis-flag real improved homes. Would need Florence's personal-property/mobile-home tax roll (a different, unbuilt source) to fix, not a reuse of this field.

South Carolina marriage licenses are issued and recorded by the county PROBATE COURT, never the Register of Deeds, statewide (state law, not county discretion) -- confirmed directly for Sumter (live-pulled its full 182-code CountyFusion/GovOS instrument-type tree: zero marriage-related codes) and corroborated by SCDHEC + Sumter's own Probate Court page. This is structurally different from NC, where RODs DO record marriage licenses (why the Johnston NC EagleWeb sweep worked). This project's ROD-platform infrastructure (sc_countyfusion.py, kofile.py, publicsearch.py, etc.) cannot reach Probate Court records at all -- a different county office entirely, not a missing filter. DIRECTLY verified only for Sumter; HIGH confidence it generalizes (state law), but not independently re-checked county-by-county.

NC tax-foreclosure sales are JUDICIAL (G.S. 105-374 in rem, or power-of-sale under G.S. 45-21.31 for mortgage-style tax foreclosures); any excess-over-debt proceeds are deposited with the CLERK OF SUPERIOR COURT inside that specific foreclosure special-proceeding's own case file, not published by the county tax office as a roster. Claiming requires a motion/petition referencing that case number (G.S. 45-21.31/105-374(q)); there is no county-wide or statewide published list of who has surplus -- confirmed independently two ways: (1) this repo's own gap_matrix.py Spec for this column already carries the ambiguity note 'SC counties publish excess-funds lists; NC clerks hold surplus without a published list', and (2) fresh 2026-11-10 web research (NC probate/estate-law firm Q&A content, a dozen+ independent articles) converges on the same claim-by-petition-to-the-case-file process with no published roster. After ~1 year unclaimed, money can migrate to the NC State Treasurer's generic Unclaimed Property Division (116B-62) -- a DIFFERENT, non-tax-sale-specific statewide database (bank accounts, uncashed checks, etc.), not a fix for this column; scraping it would need heavy filtering and is a separate future signal, not this one. This makes the 101 NC rows the gap matrix flags 'sourced-not-built' for lt_tax_sale_overage a heuristic false-positive (the matrix treats 'county has SOME tax source in county_records_matrix.json' as 'sourced' for every tax-family column, including this one, without checking that source actually publishes an overage list). Verified directly against the structural rule (judicial-foreclosure routing), not independently re-checked clerk-by-clerk for all 100 NC counties -- a county-specific override still wins if one clerk turns out to publish a list anyway.

Live-fetched https://oconeesc.com/delinquent-tax/tax-sale-information/overage-information 2026-11-10 (HTTP 200, no login/CAPTCHA): the page is PROCESS INFO ONLY, no itemized list. It states the delinquent tax office MAILS certified notification letters to anyone with available overage, and anyone else must CALL (864-638-4147) to inquire -- there is no roster of names/parcels/amounts on the page or linked from it.

The gap matrix's own 'source' pointer for this cell, https://greenvillecountysc.gov/TaxCollector/pdf/taxsaleoverbid.pdf, was live-fetched and text-extracted 2026-11-10 (HTTP 200, application/pdf): it is a static 'INSTRUCTIONS FOR FILING CLAIM FOR TAX SALE OVERAGE' form (dated 5/11/2017), not an itemized list -- no names, parcels or dollar amounts anywhere in the document. No other overage-list link found on the Tax Collector's TaxSaleProcedures/TaxSaleFAQ pages.

Live-fetched https://www.bambergcounty.sc.gov/overage-claims 2026-11-10 (HTTP 200 after a 301 from the www-less host, no login/CAPTCHA): page is claim-filing instructions only (links to an Agreement-and-Release claim FORM PDF), no itemized list of names/parcels/amounts.

Live-fetched https://jaspercountysc.gov/services/taxes/delinquent-tax-collection 2026-11-10 (HTTP 200): no document/PDF links at all on the page, no overage list. Page says the tax-sale property list itself is sold on paper ($0.50/page) at the Tax Collector's office; an overage list would require a phone call (843-717-3610) or a FOIA request, not a public scrape target.

A third-party aggregator claims Berkeley publishes 'an unclaimed tax sale overage list by owner name including bid amount and overage', but every Berkeley County path tried live 2026-11-10 with a full Chrome UA (both WebFetch and curl) -- berkeleycountysc.gov/departments/delinquent-tax/, taxsale.berkeleycountysc.gov/, and berkeleycountysc.gov/?s=overage -- returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare/WAF, not a wrong URL: all three independent paths on the same host blocked identically). This cell should read 'walled (bot check (Cloudflare/WAF))', not 'sourced-not-built'; the gap matrix has not re-detected the wall. No free/no-CAPTCHA path confirmed as of this date.

https://www.dorchestercountysc.gov/departments/delinquent-tax-collector returned HTTP 403 live 2026-11-10 (WebFetch, full browser UA) -- Cloudflare/WAF wall, same class as Berkeley above. Not re-tried via curl this session; re-verify before building.
